reflections.title: Sharing God's Good Gifts

reflect.text: When Israel set out from Mount Sinai, Moses invited his brother-in-law Hobab to travel with them. Hobab was an outsider, not an Israelite by birth. Yet Moses urged him to come along and promised to share whatever good things the Lord gave them. Moses knew that the blessings God poured out on His people were not meant to be kept to themselves. They were entrusted to Israel so they could pass them on to others.

We often think that holding tightly to what we have is the best way to stay safe. But spiritual life works the opposite way: we receive by giving. Like a riverbed that stays fresh only by letting water flow through it, our lives become stagnant if we keep God's kindness to ourselves. When we pour out what we have received, God fills us with fresh supply.

If you want to grow in faith, share it. There is no better way to learn than by telling someone else about the grace—God's undeserved kindness—that saved you. What we give away in love for God is never lost, and opening our hands to others only makes room for more of His goodness.

questions: Who in your life might need an invitation to experience God's goodness?
What is one blessing or truth God has given you that you can pass on to someone else this week?
reflections.prayer: Lord, thank You for the many good things You have given us. Please keep us from hoarding Your blessings for ourselves. Teach us to share Your truth and kindness freely with those around us, so they too may taste Your goodness. Amen.
